newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Oil jumps as U.S. inventories fall.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Oil jumps as U.S. inventories fall.

text.p: World oil prices saw gains on Wednesday after crude and gasoline inventory data from the United States came in well below expectations.
U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) statistics reiterated American Petroleum Institute (API) data overnight, with both showing considerable falls last week.
London September futures for world benchmark Brent crude oil closed 41 cents firmer at $19.00 a barrel, the highest level for the prompt contract since June 3.
"Brent has received a big lift from both the stocks numbers and gasoline prices in the U.S.," one broker said.
The API data showed U.S. crude stocks fell 9.7 million barrels last week, against an expected fall of two million barrels, while the DOE saw the crude draw at an even heftier 9.9 million barrels.

Crude stocks were showing the effects of Hurricane Danny, which forced the temporary closure of some oil fields in the Gulf of Mexico, while U.S. gasoline prices were benefiting from a combination of falling stocks and production interruptions.
Tosco Corp was forced to shut down a gasoline production unit at its 250,000 barrels per day (bpd) Bayway refinery on Wednesday after detecting a leak, a source close to the refinery said.
The New Jersey facility usually produces 130,000 bpd of gasoline.
But the persistent question mark hanging over the resumption of Iraqi oil exports under the United Nations food-for-oil deal continued to niggle brokers.
U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhart on Tuesday said the world body's review of Iraq's aid distribution plan could be completed by the end of the week.
Some of Baghdad's closest oil trading allies were confident on Wednesday that Iraqi crude exports are set to resume shortly.
